title: Key Eater report puts Azure DevOps workload trust and stolen app credentials under scrutiny
summary: Todyl reports an operator using stolen Entra application credentials, an Azure DevOps federated workload identity and replayed Azure DevOps user sessions in activity beginning 1 November 2026. Its latest update describes scripted, human-directed activity rather than a worm and states that no Microsoft vulnerability is involved. The initial credential source and any AI role remain unconfirmed; Microsoft documentation below verifies defensive controls, not the campaign.
why: Secretless pipelines still rely on the integrity of their issuing system and its resource permissions. MSP and production deployment identities deserve review alongside developer sessions, PAT exceptions and downstream credentials.
todo: Preserve available Entra, DevOps and resource logs; record gaps before rotating or removing credentials.
Review production service-connection authorization, resource checks, Azure RBAC and agent trust; do not assume WIF alone prevents abuse.
Use the related expert guide for separate user/workload Conditional Access boundaries, PAT policies and read-only hunting examples.
Treat Todyl indicators as dated investigation leads, not attribution for an entire ASN. Do not claim confirmed AI direction, initial-access mechanism or PAT abuse.
effective_note: Incident reporting, not a product rollout: Todyl source published 3 November and last updated 4 November 2026 when checked on 5 November.
